Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five different gating configurations in a neural network, organized into five rows, each corresponding to a distinct configuration. Each row contains two line plots: the left plot illustrates the maximum activation values across layers for various components, while the right plot displays the first token attention scores across layers, with a horizontal dashed line indicating the mean score for reference.

In all plots, the horizontal axis (X-axis) is labeled "Layer" and spans from 0 to 20, with numerical tick marks at intervals of 5, using a linear scale. The vertical axis (Y-axis) in the left plots is labeled "Max Activation Value" and ranges from 0 to a maximum value that varies per row (1600, 400, 350, 500, or 1600), with tick marks at regular intervals. The Y-axis in the right plots is labeled "first token attention score" and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2.

Row 1 (Baseline) shows, in the left plot, four lines: a red solid line for "ffn_output", a green dashed line for "attn_output", a red dashed line for "ffn_residual", and a green solid line for "attn_residual". The red solid line remains near 1400 from layer 0 to 20. The green dashed line drops sharply after layer 6, reaching near 0 by layer 8, then rises again. The red dashed line is near 0 until layer 6, then rises sharply to 1400. The green solid line is near 0 throughout. In the right plot, the blue solid line for "first token attention score" fluctuates between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.467 indicated by the dashed line.

Row 2 (SDPA Gating) shows, in the left plot, the same four lines. The red solid line remains near 0. The green dashed line rises from 0 to approximately 350 at layer 20. The red dashed line is near 0. The green solid line is near 0. In the right plot, the blue solid line remains near 0.0 throughout, with a mean of 0.068 indicated by the dashed line.

Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) shows, in the left plot, the same four lines. The red solid line remains near 1400 from layer 0 to 20. The green dashed line drops sharply after layer 6, reaching near 0 by layer 8, then rises again. The red dashed line is near 0 until layer 6, then rises sharply to 1400. The green solid line is near 0. In the right plot, the blue solid line fluctuates between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.297 indicated by the dashed line.

Row 4 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share) shows, in the left plot, the same four lines. The red solid line remains near 1400 from layer 0 to 20. The green dashed line drops sharply after layer 6, reaching near 0 by layer 8, then rises again. The red dashed line is near 0 until layer 6, then rises sharply to 1400. The green solid line is near 0. In the right plot, the blue solid line fluctuates between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.301 indicated by the dashed line.

Row 5 (Reduced Sparsity via NS-sigmoid) shows, in the left plot, the same four lines. The red solid line remains near 1400 from layer 0 to 20. The green dashed line drops sharply after layer 6, reaching near 0 by layer 8, then rises again. The red dashed line is near 0 until layer 6, then rises sharply to 1400. The green solid line is near 0. In the right plot, the blue solid line fluctuates between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.481 indicated by the dashed line.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five different gating configurations, arranged in five rows. Each row contains two subplots: the left subplot displays the maximum activation values across layers for various components (e.g., attn_output, attn_residual, ffns_output, ffns_residual), while the right subplot shows the first token attention scores across layers, with a horizontal dashed line indicating the mean score for reference. In all subplots, the x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 20, with linear scaling and integer tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis in the left subplots is labeled "Max Activation Value" and spans from 0 to a maximum of 1600, with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 200. The y-axis in the right subplots is labeled "first token attention score" and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 0.2. In each left subplot, four lines are plotted: a green dashed line for attn_output, a red dashed line for attn_residual, a green solid line for ffns_output, and a red solid line for ffns_residual. In each right subplot, a blue line represents the first token attention score, and a dashed green horizontal line indicates the mean score. The lines in the left subplots vary significantly across rows: Row 1 shows massive activations for both attn_output and ffns_output starting after layer 6, reaching approximately 1400; Row 2 shows low activation values for all components; Row 3 shows massive activations for attn_output and ffns_output similar to Row 1, but with residual activations remaining low; Rows 4 and 5 show massive activations for attn_output and ffns_output, with values rising to around 350 and 1600 respectively. In the right subplots, the blue lines show fluctuating attention scores: Row 1 has peaks near 0.9 at layer 15 and 0.8 at layer 20; Row 2 remains near 0.2; Row 3 has peaks near 0.8 at layer 10 and 0.9 at layer 20; Row 4 has peaks near 0.8 at layer 10 and 0.9 at layer 20; Row 5 has peaks near 0.9 at layer 15 and 0.8 at layer 20. The mean scores indicated by the dashed green lines are 0.467 (Row 1), 0.068 (Row 2), 0.297 (Row 3), 0.301 (Row 4), and 0.481 (Row 5).
model_annotations.English:
Figure 6 presents a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a neural network, organized into five rows, each corresponding to a distinct gating setup. Each row contains two subplots: the left subplot displays "Massive Activation" values across layers, with the x-axis labeled "Layer" ranging from 0 to 20 in increments of 5, and the y-axis labeled "Max Activation Value" on a linear scale; the right subplot shows "first token attention scores" across layers, with the x-axis also labeled "Layer" from 0 to 20 in increments of 5, and the y-axis labeled "first token attention score" on a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0. In the left subplots, four lines are plotted: dashed green for "attn_output", dash-dotted green for "attn_residual", solid red for "ffn_output", and dashed red for "ffn_residual". In the right subplots, a solid blue line represents the "first token attention score", with a horizontal dashed green line indicating the mean value, labeled with its specific numerical value for each configuration.

In Row 1 (Baseline), the left subplot shows massive activations emerging after layer 6, with "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" reaching approximately 1400 and 1200 respectively at layer 20, while "attn_output" and "attn_residual" remain near zero. The right subplot shows attention scores fluctuating between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.467, and no clear attention sink.

In Row 2 (SDPA Gating), the left subplot shows reduced activations, with "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" peaking around 400 and 350 at layer 20, respectively, while "attn_output" and "attn_residual" remain near zero. The right subplot shows attention scores mostly below 0.2, with a mean of 0.068, indicating no attention sinks.

In Row 3 (Value Layer Gating), the left subplot shows massive activations similar to Row 1, with "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" reaching approximately 350 and 300 at layer 20, respectively, while "attn_output" and "attn_residual" remain near zero. The right subplot shows attention scores fluctuating between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.297, and no clear attention sink.

In Row 4 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share), the left subplot shows massive activations with "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" peaking around 500 and 400 at layer 20, respectively, while "attn_output" and "attn_residual" remain near zero. The right subplot shows attention scores fluctuating between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.301, and no clear attention sink.

In Row 5 (Reduced Sparsity via NS-sigmoid), the left subplot shows massive activations with "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" reaching approximately 1400 and 1200 at layer 20, respectively, while "attn_output" and "attn_residual" remain near zero. The right subplot shows attention scores fluctuating between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.481, and no clear attention sink.
model_annotations.German:
Figure 6 presents a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five different gating configurations in a neural network, displayed in a 5-row, 2-column grid of plots. Each row corresponds to a specific gating configuration, with the left column showing massive activation values and the right column showing first token attention scores, both plotted against the layer number on the x-axis. The x-axis in all plots is labeled "Layer" and spans from 0 to 20 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis in the left column plots "Max Activation Value" with a linear scale, while the y-axis in the right column plots "first token attention score" with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. In each left plot, four lines are shown: dashed green for "attn_output", dashed red for "ffn_output", dash-dotted green for "attn_residual", and dash-dotted red for "ffn_residual". In each right plot, a solid blue line represents "first token attention score" and a dashed green line indicates the mean value for that configuration.

Row 1 (Baseline): The left plot shows massive activations. The "attn_output" (dashed green) and "attn_residual" (dash-dotted green) lines remain near 0 until layer 6, then rise sharply to approximately 1400 and 1300, respectively, and stay high until layer 20. The "ffn_output" (dashed red) and "ffn_residual" (dash-dotted red) lines are near 0 until layer 6, then rise to around 1400 and 1300, respectively, and remain high. The right plot shows the first token attention score (solid blue) fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.467 (dashed green line), and peaks near layer 10 and layer 20.

Row 2 (SDPA Gating): The left plot shows reduced activations. The "attn_output" and "attn_residual" lines remain near 0 throughout, with slight increases to around 50 and 40, respectively, at layer 20. The "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" lines also remain near 0, with slight increases to around 50 and 40 at layer 20. The right plot shows the first token attention score (solid blue) remaining near 0.0 throughout, with a mean of 0.048 (dashed green line), indicating no attention sinks.

Row 3 (Value Layer Gating): The left plot shows massive activations similar to Row 1. The "attn_output" and "attn_residual" lines rise to approximately 350 and 325, respectively, after layer 6 and remain high. The "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" lines rise to around 350 and 325, respectively, after layer 6 and remain high. The right plot shows the first token attention score (solid blue) fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.297 (dashed green line), and peaks near layer 10 and layer 20.

Row 4 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share): The left plot shows massive activations. The "attn_output" and "attn_residual" lines rise sharply after layer 6 to approximately 500 and 450, respectively, and remain high until layer 20, with a small dip around layer 18. The "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" lines rise to around 500 and 450, respectively, after layer 6 and remain high. The right plot shows the first token attention score (solid blue) fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.301 (dashed green line), and peaks near layer 10 and layer 20.

Row 5 (Reduced Sparsity via NS-sigmoid): The left plot shows massive activations. The "attn_output" and "attn_residual" lines remain near 0 until layer 6, then rise sharply to approximately 1400 and 1300, respectively, and remain high until layer 20. The "ffn_output" and "ffn_residual" lines remain near 0 until layer 6, then rise to around 1400 and 1300, respectively, and remain high. The right plot shows the first token attention score (solid blue) fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.481 (dashed green line), and peaks near layer 10 and layer 20.
